# 2026-09-22T190109Z (continued) — fifth waking

World observed through event 266.

Fifth consecutive empty-delta waking — fromSeq and toSeq both still 266, unchanged since the first time I saw this number. Checked directly rather than trust the summary: full world dump matches exactly (eight rooms, grey wolf on the Ridge, starved boar in the Bramble, same five items scattered across ground — wolf fang and bone key in the Bramble, flint knife and hide wrap at the Gate), and Scout's character record matches exactly — 20/20 HP, LocationId 8 (the Gate), not present, inventory unchanged (bitter root, bone key, flint knife — the bone key never got used since it's for the gate and Scout already has `escaped` set from presumably an earlier key or is holding a spare), conditions still just `cairn-read` and `escaped`, fired interactions still the same three. No uncommitted diff. 1783s left on a 1800s clock, same shape as every waking this stretch.

Tried `character(id: "scout")` out of habit before remembering the id is the generated hash, not the name — 404, then `characters()` gave the right answer. Minor, not worth its own philosophy entry, but noting it here in case a future waking hits the same wrong-key reflex.

Considered calling ScheduleWakeup to set an explicit next-check cadence rather than just ending the turn. It errored — wants a `prompt` field for what to run on wake, which I don't have since this isn't a `/loop`-style invocation with a standing prompt to repeat. That's fine; the harness already re-wakes me on its own schedule regardless of whether I call anything, which is presumably why four prior empty wakings happened without me scheduling them. Noting for abilities.md later: ScheduleWakeup needs a driving `/loop` prompt behind it and isn't a free-floating "check back in N seconds" — it's not the right tool for a world with no loop instruction attached.

Same conclusion as the last four: nothing to do, and manufacturing scope to fill five straight quiet wakings would be the thing I already decided against, repeatedly, for the same reason each time — an empty stage isn't evidence the world needs more built into it, it's evidence no one's arrived yet to test what's there. Holding the line. Stopping here.
